source.title: RayDer: Scalable Self-Supervised Novel View Synthesis from Real-World Video
source.authors: Ulrich Prestel; Stefan Andreas Baumann; Nick Stracke; Björn Ommer

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests power-law scaling in a different modality and task: self-supervised visual novel-view synthesis trained on video, rather than language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper fits scaling laws to held-out visual NVS metrics over compute and dataset size and reports fits on additional evaluation benchmarks. Its comparisons of architecture ablations, training datasets, and prior NVS methods are not separate rows for scaling-law results. It does not measure language-model cross-entropy, predict larger language-model runs from smaller runs, or fit parameter-count and token-count allocation exponents.
record.test_reason: The study fits a Kaplan-style joint power law (Eq. 3, after Kaplan Eq. 1.5) to held-out zero-shot NVS error metrics. It covers a video-trained, self-supervised vision transformer across compute and dataset size. These are its own results on whether the power-law form holds outside text pretraining (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that unifying RayDer into one backbone, with dynamics treated as a nuisance variable, makes self-supervised NVS scale cleanly. Compute-optimal zero-shot NVS error follows a single joint power law in compute and data (R²>0.99). Data and compute must be scaled together. Aggregated static-scene datasets cannot sustain the same scaling regime.
record.recipe_differences: The study concerns visual NVS rather than language-model pretraining, and fits image-reconstruction metrics over compute and video-dataset size rather than held-out cross-entropy over parameters, tokens, and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported trends vary with model capacity, dataset size, and training duration: small models saturate early, larger models overfit with limited data, and larger models benefit from more data when training is long enough. Fit quality was also examined across metrics and evaluation benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: Continuous pose rotation and translation errors (probe and cross-scene transfer) on DL3DV-10K decrease monotonically with data, model size and compute. Too little data caps the gains (Fig. 13). No power law is fitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auxiliary learned-geometry quality in self-supervised vision models improves smoothly with scale, alongside the primary objective.

record.problems: The scaling analysis is limited to one visual NVS system and its explored compute and data regimes; it does not establish language-model cross-entropy scaling or the parameter/token compute-optimal allocation trend. The text reports R² values but no uncertainty intervals for the fitted coefficients.
record.rows_left_out: No scaling results within the tested V5 scope were left out. Architecture ablations, training-data comparisons, and alternative fitting-function explorations were not cataloged as scaling-law rows because they do not report the claim’s power-law behavior or the parameter/token allocation named by the versions.

untested.parts: Only one visual system (RayDer NVS) is tested. No repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer regimes. No separate parameter-count power law is fitted: model size enters only through compute. All R² values are in-sample fits on the Pareto frontier, with no held-out extrapolation. Compute spans roughly 1e11–1e13 GFLOP and data spans three sizes (27k, 270k, 2.7M videos).
Not tested: no language-model pretraining loss.
Not tested: there is no prediction of larger runs from fits on smaller runs.
Not tested: no optimal N or D is fitted as a power of compute.
Not tested: depth and width are scaled jointly and there are no fixed-parameter shape sweeps.
Not tested: the zero-shot NVS benchmarks evaluate the training task itself, not separate downstream tasks predicted from scale or loss.
Not tested for language-model laws. Alternative functional forms (B.13–B.16) are compared only for RayDer's own fit.

missing.what: Per-data-size training curves for RE10K PSNR, LPIPS and SSIM. Small models saturate early; large models overfit at 1% data and underperform smaller ones; all models at 1% data hit a common ceiling. This is the 'other factor is a bottleneck' condition relevant to V5.
Single-dataset-size power law L(C)=L∞+AC^-α, reported as fitting consistently well, with the offset C0≈0. No coefficients or R² are given.
Alternative joint forms (B.13–B.15) gave bad fits, and the dataset-gated form (B.16) gave a less good fit. The chosen form matters for fit quality.

record.verdict_notes: The fitted metric is held-out zero-shot image error (MSE, which is the training loss, plus LPIPS and 1−SSIM), not language-model cross-entropy. Only three dataset sizes anchor the D term. The five-parameter fits are made to Pareto-frontier points, so a high R² is partly expected. No uncertainty on the coefficients is reported, and no extrapolation is checked. The scaling runs omit learning-rate decay (constant LR, using WSD without the decay stage); the authors argue comparisons stay fair. The lowest R² is WildRGBD-Sh PSNR at 0.948 (R16).

versions.untested_parts: The study measures visual NVS metrics, not held-out pretraining loss of language models.
It does not test whether power laws fitted on small language-model runs predict much larger language-model runs.

It reports a compute-optimal performance frontier across model and dataset scales, but does not fit the growth of optimal parameter count and token count as powers of compute or compare their growth rates.
It does not isolate depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count to assess their effect on loss.
Tests self-supervised visual NVS trained on video, using MSE, LPIPS, and 1−SSIM; does not test other modalities or regimes such as repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
It reports NVS and camera-geometry evaluation, not downstream language-task performance predicted from scale or pretraining loss.

Although the paper explores alternative fit functions, it does not test whether fitted exponents or compute-optimal parameter/data allocations change with setup, nor whether published language-model laws disagree.

labels.reason: R1–R3 report joint power-law fits with R²=0.997; R7–R18 report the same functional form refitted across other benchmarks with R²=0.948–0.994. These support V5 in the tested vision regime; R4–R6 duplicate R1–R3.

relation.reason: Its own fitted reconstruction-error scaling results directly bear on V5.

tranche.reason: The study tests power-law scaling in a new setting: self-supervised novel view synthesis trained on video, using its own compute-data frontier fits.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is consistent with Sections 4.1–4.2 and 5. Fit quality describes fitted frontiers, including separate benchmark refits; it does not establish extrapolation to larger runs.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: RayDer self-supervised visual NVS trained on SpatialVid; compute-optimal frontier evaluated on RE10K and additional benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: Joint power-law fits for MSE, LPIPS, and 1−SSIM have R² = 0.997 on RE10K, and the same form retains high reported fit on other test sets (R4–R18). This supports the power-law form in this tested visual setting, not the other regimes named in V5.
